a2-01.explain: The preterite tells what happened: finished actions, one after another. He/she form: -ar verbs add -ó (llegar > llegó, mirar > miró); -er/-ir verbs add -ió (correr > corrió, subir > subió). They form: -aron / -ieron (llegaron, corrieron). Watch out: the accent changes the meaning. Llegó = she arrived; llego = I arrive.
examples: Ana llegó tarde a la estación de Madrid.
Ana arrived late at the Madrid station.
Luego miró el andén número cuatro.
Then she looked at platform number four.
Los dos corrieron a la calle y subieron al autobús.
The two of them ran to the street and got on the bus.

a2-01.explain: Some very common verbs are irregular in the preterite. Ver > vio: like other one-syllable forms (dio, fue), it has no written accent. Decir changes its stem to dij- and ends in -o, not -ió: dijo; they: dijeron (not 'dijieron'). Learn these as whole words. Watch out: 'vió' and 'dició' are typical learner mistakes.
examples: Ana miró su teléfono y vio un mensaje de su madre.
Ana looked at her phone and saw a message from her mother.
—Perdí el tren de las nueve —dijo Ana.
"I missed the nine o'clock train," said Ana.
—¡Qué suerte! —dijo Ana.
"What luck!" said Ana.

a2-01.topic: Ir a + infinitive, and ir a + place
a2-01.explain: Ir a + infinitive talks about the near future: voy a llegar = I'm going to arrive. Ir a + place is simple movement: voy a Valencia = I'm going to Valencia. Check what follows the a: a verb means a plan, a place means a destination. Watch out: never drop the a ('voy llegar' is wrong), and a + el = al: vamos al pueblo.
examples: Perdí el tren, pero voy a llegar primero.
I missed the train, but I'm going to arrive first.
Me llamo Pablo y también voy a Valencia.
My name is Pablo and I'm going to Valencia too.
Ana va a ir a la boda de su hermana.
Ana is going to go to her sister's wedding.

a2-01.topic: Reflexive verbs: se sentó, se casa
a2-01.explain: Reflexive verbs carry a pronoun that matches the subject: me llamo, te llamas, se sentó. Some change meaning: sentar = to seat someone, sentarse = to sit down; casarse = to get married (to marry someone = casarse con alguien). The present can describe a scheduled event: se casa a las cinco = she's getting married at five. Watch out: se is not 'herself' here.
examples: Ana se sentó en un banco y lloró un poco.
Ana sat down on a bench and cried a little.
Mi hermana se casa a las cinco.
My sister is getting married at five.
Me llamo Pablo.
My name is Pablo. (lit. I call myself Pablo.)

a2-02.topic: Preterite of regular and irregular verbs
a2-02.explain: Use the preterite for finished actions in a story. Regular: abrió, salió, caminó. Irregular: ser and ir share fue, dar > dio, ver > vio (short forms, no written accent). Context tells you what fue means: fue el cumpleaños (was), fue al mercado (went). Watch out: dio and fue, not 'dió' or 'fué'.
examples: Sofía abrió la caja y vio un papel y una llave.
Sofía opened the box and saw a piece of paper and a key.
Ayer fue el cumpleaños de Sofía en Guadalajara.
Yesterday was Sofía's birthday in Guadalajara.
Doña Lupe le dio una bolsa de mangos y otro papel.
Doña Lupe gave her a bag of mangoes and another note.

a2-02.explain: To tell a friend to do something (positive tú command), use the he/she present form: busca (buscar), lleva (llevar), camina (caminar). A few common verbs have short irregular commands: ir > ve, venir > ven, hacer > haz, poner > pon, salir > sal, decir > di, tener > ten. Watch out: 'go!' is ve, not vas or va.
examples: Primero, ve al mercado y busca a doña Lupe.
First, go to the market and look for Doña Lupe.
Luego, lleva los mangos a la panadería de la plaza.
Then take the mangoes to the bakery on the square.
¡Ve!
Go!

a2-02.topic: Object pronouns: le dio, te lo regala
a2-02.explain: Indirect pronouns say to/for whom: me, te, le (to him/her/you), nos, les. They go before a conjugated verb: le dio = gave (to) her. With two pronouns, the indirect one comes first, then the direct one: te lo regala = gives it to you (lo = the puppy, el cachorro). Watch out: 'gave her a bag' is le dio, not la dio, because she receives the bag.
examples: Doña Lupe le dio una bolsa de mangos y otro papel.
Doña Lupe gave her a bag of mangoes and another note.
Ella te lo regala.
She's giving him to you (as a gift).
El panadero tomó los mangos y le dio un pan dulce.
The baker took the mangoes and gave her a sweet bun.

a2-02.explain: Time words put events in order: primero (first), luego / después (then, afterwards), entonces (then, at that moment), al final (in the end). Ayer = yesterday; por la mañana / por la tarde = in the morning / in the afternoon. Watch out: de la mañana is only used after a clock time: a las seis de la mañana = at six in the morning.
examples: Por la mañana, su abuelo Rafael llegó con una caja azul.
In the morning, her grandfather Rafael came with a blue box.
Después, corrió por la calle Hidalgo con la llave en la mano.
After that, she ran along Hidalgo Street with the key in her hand.
Entonces, un perro pequeño salió y saltó a sus brazos.
Then a small dog came out and jumped into her arms.

a2-03.explain: Mateo's cooking steps are regular preterites. -ar verbs: yo -é (tomé), he/she -ó (cortó, cocinó, probó). -er/-ir verbs: yo -í (comí), he/she -ió (decidió). Probar changes in the present (pruebo) but not in the preterite (probó). Watch out: the written accent changes the meaning. Cocinó = he cooked, cocino = I cook; tomé = I took, tomo = I take.
examples: Mateo cortó la carne y la cebolla.
Mateo cut the meat and the onion.
Mateo probó el plato.
Mateo tasted the dish.
Tomé el autobús de las seis de la mañana.
I took the six a.m. bus.

a2-03.topic: Irregular preterite: fue, puso, hice, dijo
a2-03.explain: Some key verbs have irregular preterite stems and no written accent: ir/ser > fue, poner > puso, hacer > hice (I) and hizo (he/she: c becomes z), decir > dijo. Fue can mean 'went' or 'was': fue al supermercado (went), ¿Cuál fue el secreto? (What was the secret?). Watch out: hice, not 'hací' or 'hicé'.
examples: Luego fue al supermercado y compró carne, cebolla, tomates y papas.
Then he went to the supermarket and bought meat, onion, tomatoes and potatoes.
Después, puso aceite en la sartén y cocinó la carne.
After that, he put oil in the pan and cooked the meat.
Abuela, hice tu receta, pero el sabor no es igual.
Grandma, I made your recipe, but the taste isn't the same.

a2-03.explain: Both mean 'to be', but they aren't interchangeable. Estar: location and states or impressions right now: está rico (it tastes good), estoy en la puerta. Ser: identity, characteristics and comparisons such as no es igual (it isn't the same). Watch out: some adjectives change meaning. La comida está rica = the food tastes good; el señor es rico = the man is rich.
examples: Está rico, pero no es igual.
It's tasty, but it's not the same.
Estoy en la puerta de tu casa.
I'm at the door of your house.
¿Por qué no está en el cuaderno?
Why isn't it in the notebook?

a2-03.explain: Faltar works like gustar: the missing thing is the subject. Falta algo = something is missing; for plurals use faltan: faltan dos ingredientes. Lo siento = I'm sorry (lit. I feel it). Object pronouns can attach to an infinitive: no puedo decirlo = no lo puedo decir = I can't say it. Watch out: 'I'm missing salt' is me falta sal.
examples: Falta algo.
Something is missing.
Lo siento, pero no puedo decirlo por teléfono.
I'm sorry, but I can't say it over the phone.
Solo falta un secreto.
Only one secret is missing.

a2-04.explain: The imperfect describes how things were and what used to happen: era, vivía, jugaba, tenía, tiraba. Endings: -aba for -ar verbs, -ía for -er/-ir verbs; ser is irregular (era). Siempre, todos los días and cuando era pequeño often signal it. Watch out: English 'played' can be one event or a habit; if 'used to' or 'would' fits, use the imperfect.
examples: Cuando Tomás era pequeño, vivía en un barrio pequeño de Medellín.
When Tomás was little, he lived in a small neighborhood in Medellín.
Todos los días jugaba al fútbol en la calle con su hermana Camila.
Every day he played soccer in the street with his sister Camila.
Siempre tiraba el balón a la izquierda.
She always kicked the ball to the left.

a2-04.explain: The preterite moves the story forward with completed actions: puso, saltó, paró, ganó. Some verbs have irregular stems and no accent: poner > puso, saber > supe/supiste, querer > quise. In the preterite their meaning can shift: ¿cómo lo supiste? = how did you find out / know?; quise = I wanted (and tried) to. Watch out: quise, not 'querí'.
examples: Camila puso el balón en el punto blanco.
Camila put the ball on the white spot.
Tomás saltó a la izquierda... ¡y paró el balón!
Tomás jumped to the left... and stopped the ball!
¿Cómo lo supiste?
How did you know?
Esta vez quise tirar a la derecha.
This time I wanted to kick to the right.

a2-04.explain: The imperfect sets the scene: what was going on, the weather, how people felt. The preterite gives the event that happened within it: Faltaban dos minutos (background) cuando el árbitro pitó (event). Weather uses hacer: hacía sol = it was sunny. Watch out: English 'was + -ing' or 'was' describing a scene usually means imperfect; a single action ('he blew') means preterite.
examples: Faltaban dos minutos cuando el árbitro pitó un penalti.
Two minutes were left when the referee blew his whistle for a penalty.
Hacía mucho sol y el estadio estaba lleno de gente.
It was very sunny and the stadium was full of people.
Tomás estaba muy nervioso, pero recordó algo.
Tomás was very nervous, but he remembered something.

a2-04.explain: Estar + gerund (-ar > -ando, -er/-ir > -iendo) shows an action in progress. In the imperfect (estaba esperando) it was in progress at that moment in the past. Pronouns go before estar or attach to the gerund: los estaba esperando = estaba esperándolos. Watch out: use the gerund (esperando), not the participle (esperado).
examples: Los padres y los abuelos estaban gritando y cantando.
The parents and grandparents were shouting and singing.
Su abuela los estaba esperando con un chocolate caliente.
Their grandmother was waiting for them with hot chocolate.

a2-05.explain: The imperfect paints the background before the action starts: time, weather, places, what existed. Era una tarde fría, llovía, vivía, había. Había means 'there was' and 'there were', and it stays singular: había un chico, había muchas cajas (not 'habían'). Watch out: weather and time in a description go in the imperfect (llovía, era de noche), not the preterite.
examples: Era una tarde fría de invierno en Santiago de Chile.
It was a cold winter afternoon in Santiago, Chile.
Llovía mucho y el viento golpeaba las ventanas.
It was raining a lot and the wind was beating against the windows.
Ella vivía en el número 7, y en la calle había un chico con una mochila roja.
She lived at number 7, and in the street there was a boy with a red backpack.

a2-05.explain: Form: estar + gerund (-ar > -ando, -er/-ir > -iendo; leer > leyendo). It describes an action in progress; with estaba, it was in progress at that past moment. A gerund can also show how someone did something: bajó corriendo = she hurried out (lit. got out running). Watch out: Spanish doesn't use this form for plans: 'I'm working tomorrow' = trabajo mañana.
examples: Valentina estaba en su sala, tomando té y mirando una serie.
Valentina was in her living room, drinking tea and watching a series.
Estaba trabajando y mi teléfono nuevo no tenía batería.
I was working and my new phone had no battery.
La mamá de Nicolás bajó corriendo con las llaves en la mano.
Nicolás's mother hurried out of the car with the keys in her hand.

a2-05.explain: The preterite gives the actions that happen against the background: sonó, leyó, respondió, salió. Phrases like de repente (suddenly) and un minuto después point to a single event. Spelling: when the stem ends in a vowel, -ió becomes -yó: leer > leyó, oír > oyó. Watch out: 'leió' is wrong.
examples: De repente, su teléfono sonó.
Suddenly, her phone rang.
Valentina leyó el mensaje dos veces.
Valentina read the message twice.
Salió de casa y caminó hasta la puerta azul.
She left the house and walked to the blue door.

a2-05.explain: Reflexive verbs use a pronoun that matches the subject (me, te, se, nos, se): levantarse (get up), sentarse (sit down), ponerse (put on), llamarse (be called). With clothes and body parts Spanish uses el/la, not a possessive: se puso el abrigo = she put on her coat. Watch out: without se, puso el abrigo just means she put the coat somewhere.
examples: Valentina se levantó y miró por la ventana.
Valentina got up and looked out of the window.
Luego se puso el abrigo y tomó un paraguas.
Then she put on her coat and took an umbrella.
Se llamaba Nicolás y tenía trece años.
His name was Nicolás and he was thirteen years old.

a2-06.explain: La is a direct object, 'her' or 'it' for a feminine noun: la abrazó = hugged her; la guardó = kept it (the lamp). Le is indirect: to/for him or her. Gustar works backwards: the thing liked is the subject, so a Camila le gustaba el edificio = the building pleased Camila. Watch out: the verb agrees with the thing (le gustaban las ventanas), and you need the a: a Camila.
examples: —Mamá la guardó para ti —le explicó él.
"Mom kept it for you," he explained to her.
Camila se puso a llorar un poco, y Tomás la abrazó.
Camila started to cry a little, and Tomás hugged her.
El edificio era viejo, pero a Camila le gustaba mucho.
The building was old, but Camila liked it a lot.

a2-06.explain: The tú command is usually the he/she present form, stem change included: probar > prueba. Pronouns attach to the end of a positive command, and a written accent keeps the original stress: prueba + la = pruébala (try it); di + me + lo = dímelo (tell me). Watch out: don't split them ('prueba la') or put them first: la prueba means 'she tries it'.
examples: Si necesitas ayuda, dímelo.
If you need help, tell me.
Es para ti. Pruébala.
It's for you. Try it.
Ayúdame con las cajas.
Help me with the boxes.

a2-06.explain: Many everyday reflexives describe moving, sitting and changes: mudarse (to move house), sentarse (to sit down), encenderse (to turn on by itself: la lámpara no se encendió). Ponerse a + infinitive means 'to start doing something': se puso a llorar = she started crying. Watch out: mudarse is for moving house; moving your body is moverse.
examples: Camila se mudó a un apartamento nuevo en Santiago el sábado por la mañana.
Camila moved into a new apartment in Santiago on Saturday morning.
Camila se puso a llorar un poco, y Tomás la abrazó.
Camila started to cry a little, and Tomás hugged her.
Camila puso la lámpara sobre la mesa, pero no se encendió.
Camila put the lamp on the table, but it didn't turn on.

a2-06.explain: Ir (voy, vas, va, vamos, van) + a + infinitive says what is going to happen. Vamos a + infinitive can also mean 'let's': vamos a subir todo = we're going to / let's carry everything up. A pronoun attaches to the infinitive or goes before ir: va a darte = te va a dar (is going to give you). Watch out: don't drop the a.
examples: Vamos a subir todo por la escalera.
We're going to carry everything up the stairs.
Esta lámpara va a darte luz y alegría.
This lamp is going to give you light and joy.
Voy a comprar una ahora mismo.
I'm going to buy one right now.

a2-07.explain: Use the imperfect for routines and repeated actions (tocaba, llegaba, se sentaba), often with todas las tardes or siempre. Use the preterite for a single event that breaks the routine (empezó, se rompió, volvió), often with un jueves, de repente or diez minutos después. Watch out: English 'played' can be either; ask whether it was a habit or one occasion.
examples: Todas las tardes, Mateo tocaba la guitarra en una plaza de San Telmo, en Buenos Aires.
Every afternoon, Mateo played the guitar in a square in San Telmo, in Buenos Aires.
Un jueves, Mateo empezó una canción y de repente se rompió una cuerda.
One Thursday, Mateo started a song and suddenly a string broke.
Pero diez minutos después, la niña volvió con un señor de pelo blanco.
But ten minutes later, the girl came back with a white-haired man.

a2-07.explain: Indirect pronouns say to/for whom: me contó = told me; le cambió la cuerda = changed the string for him. When le or les comes before lo/la/los/las, it becomes se: se la mostró = showed it (la guitarra) to him; never 'le la'. Pronouns can attach to an infinitive, indirect first: pagártelo = to pay you for it.
examples: Ella me contó que tocas muy bien.
She told me you play very well.
Mateo se la mostró.
Mateo showed it to him.
Ernesto le cambió la cuerda en cinco minutos.
Ernesto changed the string for him in five minutes.
Quiero pagártelo.
I want to pay you for it.

a2-07.explain: Más + adjective + que = more ... than / -er than: más vieja que yo = older than me. After que, use subject pronouns (yo, tú), not mí or ti. Bueno has an irregular comparative, mejor (better); with a possessive or article it means 'best': su mejor alumna = his best student. Watch out: for quality say mejor, not 'más bueno'.
examples: Es muy bonita, pero es más vieja que yo.
It's very pretty, but it's older than I am.
Es más bonita que la radio.
It's prettier than the radio.
Julieta es su mejor alumna.
Julieta is his best student.

a2-07.explain: Positive tú commands usually match the he/she present: toca (play), toma (take; also 'here you go'). Venir is irregular: ven (come). Context shows whether toca is a command (¡Toca para nosotros!) or a statement (Mateo toca en la plaza). Watch out: ven, not 'viene' or 'vienes'. In Buenos Aires you'll also hear vos commands: vení, tocá, tomá.
examples: Ven conmigo a la tienda.
Come with me to the shop.
Toca para nosotros.
Play for us.
—Toma —le dijo.
"Here you go," he said to him.

a2-08.explain: The imperfect describes background and actions in progress (había, caminaba, pensaba); the preterite tells completed events (se puso, cubrió, llegaron). The preterite can also sum up a closed period as a whole: durante la mañana, el paisaje fue precioso = the scenery was beautiful (all morning). Watch out: 'was' can be fue or era; are you summing up a finished period, or describing?
examples: Jairo caminaba delante, pero Andrés se paró a atarse las botas.
Jairo was walking ahead, but Andrés stopped to tie his boots.
Al mediodía, el cielo se puso gris y una niebla blanca cubrió el camino.
At noon, the sky turned gray and a white fog covered the path.
Durante la mañana, el paisaje fue precioso.
During the morning, the scenery was beautiful.

a2-08.explain: Positive tú commands use the he/she present form, stem changes included: camina, escucha, sigue (seguir), recuerda (recordar), prueba (probar). A pronoun attaches at the end, with an accent: pruébalo (try it). Watch out: in Lo importante es no correr, correr is an infinitive ('not to run'), not a command; a negative tú command has its own form (no corras).
examples: Si hay niebla, camina despacio y sigue el río.
If there is fog, walk slowly and follow the river.
Recuerda lo que dijo Jairo.
Remember what Jairo said.
Pruébalo.
Try it.

a2-08.explain: Ponerse + adjective means 'to become / get' (a change of state): se puso nervioso = he got nervous; el cielo se puso gris = the sky turned gray. The pronoun matches the subject: vamos a levantarnos (we). Se oía el viento is a different se: no person is named, so it means 'the wind could be heard'. The verb agrees with what is heard: se oían los pájaros.
examples: Andrés se puso nervioso.
Andrés got nervous.
Mañana vamos a levantarnos a las seis.
Tomorrow we're going to get up at six.
Solo se oía el viento.
Only the wind could be heard.

a2-08.explain: Más + adjective + que = more ... than; mejor que = better than. Superlative: el/la/los/las (+ noun) + más + adjective + de: las palmas más altas del mundo = the tallest palms in the world (de, not en). Tan + adjective + que = so ... that. Watch out: tan ... como means 'as ... as': tan alto como tú.
examples: Valle de Cocora, donde crecen las palmas más altas del mundo.
The Cocora Valley, where the tallest palm trees in the world grow.
Es mejor que el chocolate de mi casa.
It's better than the hot chocolate at my house.
Andrés estaba tan asustado que no podía pensar.
Andrés was so scared that he couldn't think.

a2-09.explain: Imperfect = background and what was going on (esperaba, repasaba, la entrevista era a las diez). Preterite = the events, one after another (se despertó, chocó, ayudé). Mientras (while) usually introduces an ongoing action in the imperfect, and another event can interrupt it. Watch out: 'while I was waiting' is mientras esperaba, not 'mientras esperé'.
examples: Mientras esperaba el metro, repasaba sus respuestas en voz baja.
While she was waiting for the subway, she was going over her answers under her breath.
Daniela se despertó a las ocho y media, porque su alarma no sonó.
Daniela woke up at eight thirty because her alarm didn't go off.
Mi alarma no sonó, un señor me tiró un café encima y después ayudé a una señora.
My alarm didn't go off, a man spilled coffee on me, and then I helped a lady.

a2-09.explain: Form: he, has, ha, hemos, han + participle (-ar > -ado, -er/-ir > -ido); with usted it's ha: ¿ha trabajado? It links the past to now, especially life experience: nunca he llegado tarde = I've never been late. The participle never changes, and nothing goes between he and it. Watch out: 'I've been looking for 20 minutes' is llevo veinte minutos buscándola (present of llevar + gerund).
examples: Nunca he llegado tarde a una entrevista.
I've never been late for an interview.
¿Ha trabajado antes con clientes?
Have you worked with clients before? (usted)
¿Qué ha pasado?
What's happened?
Llevo veinte minutos buscándola.
I've been looking for it for twenty minutes.

a2-09.explain: Reflexive verbs carry a pronoun that matches the subject: me desperté, te despertaste, se despertó. Many daily-routine verbs are reflexive: despertarse (to wake up), vestirse (to get dressed; e > i: se vistió), sentarse (to sit down). Ponerse + adjective means 'to become': no se puso nerviosa = she didn't get nervous. Watch out: without se the verb needs an object and means doing it to someone else: despertó a su hermana = she woke her sister up; vistió al niño = she dressed the child.
examples: Daniela se despertó a las ocho y media, porque su alarma no sonó.
Daniela woke up at eight thirty because her alarm didn't go off.
Se vistió rápidamente, tomó su currículum y salió corriendo de casa.
She got dressed quickly, grabbed her résumé and ran out of the house.
La señora mayor entró en la sala y se sentó junto a la jefa.
The older woman came into the room and sat down next to the boss.

a2-09.explain: Tú is informal; usted is formal and uses the he/she verb form: (usted) llega tarde = you're late, but (tú) llegas tarde. The interviewer, Mrs. Ortega, uses usted with Daniela the whole time (llega, tiene, ¿ha trabajado?, el puesto es suyo); Daniela is polite to the older woman too (la acompaño). The older woman and the man at the metro use tú (¿sabes?, no te vi), and so does the founder later (tú me ayudaste). Watch out: llega, tiene or suyo can mean 'he/she/his/her' or 'you/yours (usted)'; context decides.
examples: —Llega tarde —dijo—, y tiene la camisa manchada.
"You're late," she said, "and your shirt is stained."
Hija, ¿sabes dónde está la oficina de diseño?
Dear, do you know where the design office is?
Perdona, no te vi.
Sorry, I didn't see you.
El puesto es suyo.
The position is yours. (usted)

a2-10.explain: Imperfect for habits and background (cada agosto viajaba, hacían, llevaban, tenía); preterite for single completed events (empezó, llovió, hiciste). Empezar a + infinitive = to start doing: empezó a llover. Hiciste is the irregular preterite of hacer (tú). Watch out: cada año or todos los días usually signal the imperfect; el viernes por la noche marks one event.
examples: Todos los vecinos hacían faroles de papel y los llevaban por las calles al anochecer.
All the neighbors made paper lanterns and carried them through the streets at dusk.
El viernes por la noche empezó a llover.
On Friday night it started to rain.
Hoy no hiciste solo un farol, Inés.
Today you didn't just make a lantern, Inés.

a2-10.explain: Más + adjective + que compares two things: más bonito que antes = prettier than before. The superlative is el/la + noun + más + adjective + de: el farol más grande de la historia = the biggest lantern in history. Watch out: English says 'in', Spanish says de: la fiesta más importante del pueblo = the most important festival in the village.
examples: Era más bonito que antes.
It was prettier than before.
Es el farol más grande de la historia del pueblo.
It's the biggest lantern in the history of the village.
Hiciste una familia más grande.
You made a bigger family.

a2-10.topic: Object pronouns: se lo, le, la
a2-10.explain: La = her (direct object): la ayudó = helped her. Le = to/for him or her (indirect). With body parts Spanish uses le + the article, not a possessive: le tomó la mano = took her hand. When le/les meets lo/la, it becomes se: se lo contó a los vecinos = told it to the neighbors (lo = what had happened). Watch out: never 'le lo' or 'les lo'.
examples: Pablo salió a la calle y se lo contó a los vecinos.
Pablo went out into the street and told the neighbors about it.
Su abuelo se acercó y le tomó la mano.
Her grandfather came over and took her hand.
Su primo Pablo la ayudó.
Her cousin Pablo helped her.

a2-10.topic: Perfect tenses: he visto, había aprendido
a2-10.explain: Present perfect: he/has/ha + participle, for experience up to now: nunca he visto = I have never seen. Past perfect: había + participle, for something that happened before another past moment: había aprendido = she had learned. The participle never changes. Watch out: some participles are irregular: visto (ver), hecho (hacer), dicho (decir), puesto (poner).
examples: Nunca he visto trabajar tan rápido a este pueblo.
I've never seen this village work so fast.
Había aprendido que un pueblo unido puede hacer cosas increíbles.
She had learned that a united village can do incredible things.
Cuando Inés llegó al granero, la lluvia ya había mojado el papel.
When Inés got to the barn, the rain had already soaked the paper.
